text: Roguing (ការកាត់ពូជលាយ) is the practice of walking the seed field and physically pulling out any rice plant - or weed - that shows different characteristics (phenotype) from the target variety, so the harvested seed lot stays true-to-type. It is done at three points in the season, and any suspect plant should always be pulled and destroyed on the spot rather than left standing to check again later. Round 1, from tillering through stem elongation: check tillering habit, plant and leaf color, and plant height against the rest of the field. Round 2, from panicle emergence/flowering through the milk stage: check heading time (plants that head noticeably earlier or later than the rest), plant height, stem color, leaf color, flag leaf length, leaf angle, panicle exsertion, panicle shape, grain color, grain length (longer or shorter than normal), and presence or absence of awns. Round 3, about 15 days (roughly two weeks) before harvest: check panicle shape, grain size (unusually small or large), and panicle length, along with re-checking the same traits noted in Rounds 1 and 2. The general rule farmers are taught: if a plant shows any trait that looks different from what's expected of the variety, remove it immediately rather than leaving it in the field.
